newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end up on select blue-chip buying.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end up on select blue-chip buying.

text.p: Select blue-chip buying by local financial institutions continued through the day, helping the key Composite Index end with fresh gains on Monday, brokers and analysts said.
They said volume was low and foreign investors remained absent from the market.
"It seems like selective local institutional buying," said a foreign resarch analyst based in Kuala Lumpur. "The flows from New York and London have been pretty disappointing."
At the close, the Composite Index was up 13.14 points or 1.19 percent at 1,117.97
Brokers said much of the buying was focused on big issues like Tenaga, which rose 40 cents to 11.90 ringgit and Sime Darby, which was up 15 cents to 8.35 ringgit.
Telekom, trading ex-bonus of one share for every two held, was at 12.60 ringgit, 20 cents higher than its implied price of 12.40. It ended at 18.60 ringgit on Friday.
The retail-focused second board, however, experienced some profit-taking and its index ended down 4.43 points at 565.02.
This indicated that the buying was not broad-based, the analysts said.
"Last week, the speculative issues and second board stocks led the rise. Now the market is relooking at some blue-chips," said a sales executive at an asset management firm.
"It is good to see the Composite Index staying above 1,080 for so long. Seems like sentiment has genuinely improved," she said.
She added that with Composite Index futures contract once again trading at a premium to the cash market, the cash market could make more gains in the next few days.
The June contract on the Kuala Lumpur Options and Financial Futures Exchange ended up 27.5 points at 1,134.5.
"I think we have seen quite a strong recovery since 1,020 (on May 16). I don't see much scope to push beyond perhaps the 1,150," Simon Maughan, head of research at W.I.Carr in Kuala Lumpur.
The volume for the day was 218.5 million shares. Gainers trailed losers 194 to 395.
